doc.title: Eddie Palmieri — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Latin music history and the Palladium
title: Starting at the Palladium in 1956 with Vicentico Valdes
summary: He joined Vicentico Valdes's conjunto at the Palladium, with Mongo Santamaria and Manny Oquendo; conjunto versus orchestra.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: But throughout the ‘50s... I started working the Palladium in 1956 with Vicentico Valdés, who was the vocalist for Tito Puente, when my brother was in the band, and Mongo

Santamaria was the conga player. Manny Oquendo, bongo. An incredible conjunto. Conjunto meant that there was no saxes. That’s what it meant. Only Machito had an orchestra. Tito Puente was a conjunto—three trumpets and a rhythm section...timbales, conga, bongo, bass naturally, piano, and three trumpets.
We’ll talk about genres later, how charanga developed and things like that.
